basis: FERC-certified on-site gas-turbine generating plant (240 MW) — real gas-fired electricity, ~4.8x the >50 MW GOGPT threshold. Single-origin regulatory (FERC order + FEIS are both FERC); no independent trade restatement of the exact number, but a lone primary/regulatory source is green.
mechanical_drive_note: SEPARATE, NOT in the 240 MW: 4x GE Frame 7 gas turbines drive 8 refrigerant compressors + 2 electric-motor boost compressors (Phase 1); shaft MW not disclosed. Never sum into the generating MW.

electric_mw: undisclosed — do not populate; >50 MW only scale-inferred from 22.5 Mtpa
basis: On-site gas-fired cogeneration integral to the ConocoPhillips Optimized Cascade design; existence well-corroborated (3 independent publishers) but NO public MW anywhere and project is pre-FERC-file -> a proposed GOGPT record with an unpopulated capacity. TCEQ NSR air permit is the doc most likely to carry per-turbine MW; re-check.
mechanical_drive_note: Compressor-driver architecture unconfirmed; reads as electricity-generating cogeneration but no source rules out gas-turbine mechanical drive.

electric_mw: undisclosed — waste-heat steam-turbine cogen generator set(s), MW not published; + emergency-only engine gensets
basis: Only continuous on-site electricity is waste-heat steam-turbine cogeneration (HRSGs on the six Frame 7EA feed Siemens STG sets) with no published nameplate; largest on-site MW is mechanical drive (non-electric). Decision: track a cogen plant with an unsourceable nameplate, or hold until an MW surfaces?
mechanical_drive_note: SEPARATE, NOT electricity: 6x GE/Baker Hughes MS7001EA (Frame 7EA) shaft-drive 12 refrigerant compressors, ~515 MW aggregate shaft (per-unit ~86 MW inferred, not PASS-verified). The 3x 6.8-MW BOG motors are electrical LOAD, not generation.

electric_mw: none — operating power from the AEP 138 kV grid; only on-site gen is ~16.35 MW diesel emergency (6x 2,725 kW), non-gas
basis: FERC FEIS is unambiguous: operating power comes from the AEP grid (new transmission line + switchyard), not self-generation; only on-site electricity is emergency diesel. The large gas turbines are mechanical drive for compressors. Secondary '300 MW generators' / 'self-powered' claims are contradicted by the FERC record and were not used.
mechanical_drive_note: SEPARATE, NOT electricity: 2x Baker Hughes Frame 7 gas turbines per train drive centrifugal refrigerant compressors (Trains 1-3 = 6; Trains 4 & 5 = +2 each); per-turbine MW not in any verified source.

electric_mw: none — Trains 1-3 mechanical drive; Stage 3 grid electric-motor; only on-site gen is ~0.75 MW/unit diesel standby
basis: No gas-fired electricity generation: Trains 1-3 have no gensets, Stage 3 compressor power is imported from the transmission grid (electric-motor drive), only on-site generators are diesel standby. FERC Stage 3 EA + EPA GHG permit primary.
mechanical_drive_note: SEPARATE, NOT electricity: Trains 1-3 = 18x GE LM2500 G4+ / Baker Hughes PGT25+G4 (6/train), ~34 MW-class ISO shaft each (~600 MW aggregate shaft). Any aggregate 'power station MW' from a turbine count would conflate shaft power with electricity.
